title: Elite Beat Agents
subtitle: Help arrives on the beat
summary: Elite Beat Agents is iNiS's Nintendo DS rhythm game about a secret team sent to encourage people through moments of crisis. Commander Kahn dispatches the dancing agents into a series of comic-book situations, from everyday troubles to increasingly extravagant emergencies. body: Elite Beat Agents is iNiS's Nintendo DS rhythm game about a secret team sent to encourage people through moments of crisis. Commander Kahn dispatches the dancing agents into a series of comic-book situations, from everyday troubles to increasingly extravagant emergencies. The player follows popular songs through tapping, dragging and spinning actions on the touchscreen. Made as an international counterpart to Osu! Tatakae! Ouendan, it replaces that game's Japanese setting and music with a new cast, stories and licensed songs recorded as in-game covers.

Numbered circles appear across the lower screen, with closing rings indicating when to tap. Other patterns ask the stylus to follow a moving marker or spin repeatedly. The upper screen shows the current story and the agents' encouragement, letting musical performance alter how the situation develops. The player has to listen as well as follow the visual sequence. A familiar song provides a structure to anticipate, while the changing placement of targets turns that structure into a small physical routine performed with the hand.

The short stories give a missed beat an immediate comic consequence: the person being helped can struggle or recover as the performance changes. That feedback ties a scoring challenge to a visible reason for playing well. Different difficulty levels rearrange the demands of a song, allowing an already familiar scene to support another attempt. Elite Beat Agents makes its encouragement unusually generous. The spectacle belongs to the characters above, but the repeated, precise gestures below are what allow their unlikely rescue to keep moving.
